Definition: Ijob, the patriarch famous for his patience
BiblicalUsage: Job is the man whose patience James holds up, and the book that bears his name tells his story. In Job 1:1 there is a man in the land of Uz, whose name is Job, and that man is perfect and upright, and one that feareth God, and escheweth evil, in Job 1:8 the LORD asks Satan, hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, and in Ezekiel 14:14 God names Noah, Daniel, and Job as the three righteous men who could only deliver their own souls.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Job's story is the hardest in the Bible and the most honest: a righteous man who loses everything, and a God who answers him out of the whirlwind.
RelatedEvents: Job's Suffering and Restoration; Job's Losses in a Single Day
